summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and anxiety presented with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was managed conservatively with IV fluids, pain control, and anti-nausea medications. Her symptoms improved rapidly, allowing advancement to a soft diet and transition to oral medications. She remained pain-free by discharge, was ambulatory, and expressed readiness to return home. She was discharged with instructions to slowly advance her diet, avoid alcohol, and monitor for recurrent symptoms, with prescriptions for prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, and continued management of her psychiatric and gastrointestinal conditions.
